subject: Dedicated capacity inquiry — Aurora Health
messages:
From: Mina Rao <mina.rao@aurorahealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity inquiry — Aurora Health

Hi Logan / Marissa,

We're starting to map out a dedicated inference deployment for a patient-facing summarization feature and want an initial sizing conversation. High level:
- Traffic pattern: steady during business hours (08:00–20:00 ET), with potential evening spikes during clinical rollouts.
- Estimated active users at launch: 20k MAU; expected peak concurrent users ~150 (web + mobile).
- Workload: 350–450 token prompts, ~600–1,200 token responses on average.
- SLA: 95th pctile latency targets under 1s for short requests; tail can be slower for long reports.
- Data residency: US only, PHI-sensitive (we'll need guidance on Private deployment & KMS).

I've attached a small sample of typical prompts and a csv with request size histogram. Could you run a quick intake and tell us what a minimum viable dedicated footprint looks like to start (sku recommendations, buffers for scaling, any obvious gotchas)? Also include any required items our security/procurement team will ask for.

Attch: workload_sample.csv (CSV)

Thanks,
Mina Rao
Product Lead — Clinical AI
Aurora Health

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Mina Rao <mina.rao@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-05T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — Aurora Health

Hi Mina — thanks for the detail, this is great and a good place to start.

Quick next steps I recommend:
1) Please complete the short attached sizing questionnaire (we use it to convert token distributions to qps/concurrency).
2) Share any peak-hour historical logs if available (if not, the csv you sent is fine).
3) I'd like to schedule a 30 min sizing call with our pre-sales team to run through the numbers and align on deployment mode (Dedicated vs Private).

High level thoughts based on what you sent: for 150 peak concurrent users with the response lengths you cited, expect to need a multi-GPU setup to meet sub-1s 95th latency for short interactions and to keep cost predictable. We'll size both a baseline (MVP) and a rollout plan that increases throughput with predictable step-ups.

I've attached our questionnaire to speed the process — once you return it, Marissa will produce a quick preliminary fleet sketch (skus, vCPU/memory assumptions, and an estimated committed footprint).

Calendar link: https://cal.com/logan/30min?c=aurora

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-sizing-questionnaire.pdf

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Mina Rao <mina.rao@aurorahealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-07T08:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — Aurora Health

Logan / Marissa — thanks. I filled the questionnaire and added more detail inline. Summary here:
- Peak QPS (short requests, ~<200 tokens): 45 qps peak
- Sustained business-hour qps: ~12–18 qps
- Target concurrency: 20–40 concurrent model sessions for interactive UI; up to 120 concurrent for batch summarization jobs (nightly).
- Prompt tokens (median): 360; response tokens (median): 820; 99th percentile response length ~2,100 tokens for full record exports.
- Batch jobs: average 1,200 requests per night, processed in a 3-hour window (elastic burst ok).
- Retention: 30 days, encrypted at-rest and in-transit; PHI will require KMS-managed keys and SOC2 evidence.
- Preferred region: us-east-1.

Attached: aurora-workload-profile.csv (detailed histogram + example payload sizes).

Cc'ing Aaron Lin from our infra for procurement coordination.

Thanks,
Mina

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mina Rao <mina.rao@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-07T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — Aurora Health

Mina — appreciate the fast turnaround and the detailed profile. I sketched a preliminary footprint based on the distributions you provided (see attached). Highlights:

- MVP: 3 x A100 80GB equivalents (or 4 x H100 80GB if you prefer headroom for long-context 2k+ responses). This configuration aims to hit ~95th % <1s for short requests at 45 qps with target concurrency headroom of ~1.5x.
- Batch window: allow autoscaled burst to an extra 2 GPUs for the nightly jobs (3-hour window) — can be scheduled as transient capacity to avoid long-term commitment.
- Memory/kv cache: for long 2k+ token responses we recommend enabling shard-aware KV caching and quantized checkpoints (we handle kernel selection automatically in Dedicated).
- Security/Procurement: we'll provide SOC2 artifact pack, KMS integration guide, and a draft mutual action plan (MAP). For PHI you should plan for Private deployment (control plane in your VPC) or a Dedicated-isolated tenancy with customer-managed KMS.
- Rough cost/commit: for the MVP footprint above expect an initial reserved commit estimate in the $65k–$90k/month range depending on SKU choices and uplift for H100 vs A100.

Next steps:
- Confirm whether you'd prefer A100 vs H100 pricing trade-offs (we'll attach a side-by-side).
- If procurement is ready, send over your preferred contract cadence (monthly vs annual) and any security questionnaire items beyond SOC2 / KMS.

Attachment: prelim-fleet-proposal.xlsx

Hi Marissa / Logan,

Thanks for the proposal. Procurement here — to move forward we need:
- Draft SOW and pricing for both A100 and H100 options (monthly and annual commit).
- Sample MAP with milestones and acceptance criteria.
- SOC2 report and a KMS architecture diagram (how customer keys are used).
- Any standard redlines you will not accept (we need to know limits for our legal team).

We are tentatively OK with the sizing sketch; please route the SOW and contract artifacts to procurement@aurorahealth.com and CC Mina / Aaron. Also attach the SLA_request.pdf with uptime/latency SLOs.
